newsitem.title: USA: Payless to buy back 460,000 of its shares.
newsitem.headline: Payless to buy back 460,000 of its shares.

text.p: Payless ShoeSource Inc said Tuesday its directors authorized the repurchase of 460,000 shares or about one percent of its 40.4 million common shares outstanding.
Based on a September 9, 1996 closing price of $34-3/8, the repurchase program would cost $15.8 million.

The repurchase program is designed to avoid the dilutive impact of shares issued under the company's benefit plans, the footwear retailer said in a statement. The repurchased shares will be held in the treasury for general corporate purposes, it said.
Repurchases will be made in the open market from time to time before the program expires August 1, 1997 and may be discontinued at any time, the company said.

Payless ShoeSource operates 4,257 stores in 50 states, Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands. The retailer was a division of May Department Stores Co until May 4, 1996 when it was spun off to shareholders as an independent company.
